content.rendered:
We’re taking the way-way-WAY-back machine today:

“Will You Love Me Tomorrow,” written and recorded by Carole King, covered here by…

Dr. Zoom and the Sonic Boom!

Bruce’s shortest-lived band, Dr. Zoom and the Sonic Boom lasted all of two gigs, but it’s not hard to hear glimmers of the future E Street Band: Bruce, Stevie, Garry, Vini, and David Sancious are already present, and while the Big Man hadn’t yet made the scene, there are saxophones (two) in the house.

On stage, there were almost as many backup singers as musicians, and while you’re picturing that assemblage while you listen to this performance,  add to your mental vision an on-stage Monopoly game and baton twirler (seriously), and you’ll pretty much have the scene captured.

(Note: I realize that this song was originally recorded by The Shirelles in 1960, but this arrangement is far more similar to Carole King’s version on Tapestry. Given that Tapestry was released in February 1971, just a few months before this Dr. Zoom performance, I’m inclined to think that Bruce had Carole’s version in mind rather than the original Shirelles recording. And since Carole also co-wrote the song, I’m crediting this cover to her.)

Will You Love Me Tomorrow
First performed: May 15, 1971 (Union, NJ)
Last performed: January 17, 1990 (New York City, NY)

© January 20, 2018

jetpack-related-posts.title: Alexander’s Ragtime Band (Zoom Theme)
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Half a century ago and twice only (thankfully): Bruce adapted Irving Berlin's 1911 classic as the short-lived theme song for Dr. Zoom and the Sonic Boom.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Southside Shuffle
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One time only: Bruce turns the spotlight on Southside Johnny when Dr. Zoom and the Sonic Boom play the only known performance of "Southside Shuffle."

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jumbeliah
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: "Jumbeliah" marks a transition in Bruce's songwriting and provides a fascinating look at one of the only original compositions he created for the short-lived Dr. Zoom and the Sonic Boom.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lady of Boston
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One time only: Dr. Zoom and the Sonic Boom let loose (and I do mean loose) with the transitional "Lady of Boston."

jetpack-related-posts.title: It Takes a Lot to Laugh, It Takes a Train to Cry
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Performed only twice, way back in 1971: Dr. Zoom and the Sonic Boom covers Bob Dylan's "It Takes a Lot to Laugh, It Takes a Train to Cry."

jetpack-related-posts.title: Last Night in Texas
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Let's kick off summer with Dr. Zoom and the Sonic Boom in this rewritten version of Sonny Boy Williamson's "One Way Out."
